findings.title: queued default evaluated once at import
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py the dataclass defines `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. Dataclass defaults are evaluated once at class definition time, so every AssignmentSource instance shares the same timestamp from import. Any recency/expiry/debounce logic using `queued` will be wrong. It must be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

findings.title: AssignmentSource datetime not safe for Celery kwargs round-trip
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py `to_dict()` returns `asdict(self)` including a raw `datetime` for `queued`. That dict is passed as `assignment_source_dict` to `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async` in src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py. Celery task kwargs must be JSON-serializable; a datetime will fail serialization or arrive as an ISO string. `from_dict()` then does `cls(**input_dict)` without parsing strings, so a round-tripped value becomes a `str` where `datetime` is expected, breaking type invariants and any time comparison.

findings.title: Corrupt source dict fails open and re-enables cycle
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py an unparseable `assignment_source_dict` makes `AssignmentSource.from_dict()` return None, and the code then calls `should_sync` with None, i.e. no source. That permits outbound sync back to the integration that originated the inbound change, exactly the loop this PR claims to fix. A parse failure should fail closed (skip/log) rather than silently dropping loop protection.

findings.title: should_sync signature change breaks existing overrides
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py `should_sync` was changed from `should_sync(attribute)` to `should_sync(attribute, sync_source=None)` and the outbound task now calls it with two positional arguments. Any existing IssueBasicIntegration/IssueSyncIntegration subclass that overrides the old one-argument signature will raise TypeError when called with the new argument, breaking outbound sync for that provider. The base call needs backward-compatible handling for overrides that do not accept the new parameter.
